soundness_flags.label: prop:rank-interval-projection
soundness_flags.one_line: Once the true weak order lies in the reported set, containment of each true tied-rank interval in the union-defined rank set follows by definition, so this should be a corollary/reporting remark rather than an independent proposition.

source_verification_receipts.version: Statistical and Probability Letters 105 (2015), author manuscript reflecting the published article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes binary stratified interference and forms exact confidence sets for scalar effects by inverting compatible sharp-null permutation tests.
The cited article exists at the stated venue and studies simultaneous confidence sets for ranks under weak assumptions.
The article develops finite-sample rank confidence sets by exploiting multinomial structure.

source_verification_receipts.version: NBER working-paper source corresponding to the published JASA article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper validates artificial experiments that make originally non-sharp interference nulls sharp for randomization analysis.

The primary version studies finite-sample conditional tests for partially sharp and bounded individual-level nulls, asymptotic weak-average tests, and a finite-sample unconditional test of global monotonicity across saturation levels.
The paper specifies complete randomization at both stages and gives covariance, conservative-variance, asymptotic-normality, and asymptotic-test results.

source_verification_receipts.version: Preprint corresponding to Annals of Statistics 42(3) (2014), 850-871
source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract; Lemma 1 and Proposition 1 in the article text
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives sharp variance bounds and asymptotic sharpness for completely randomized experiments.
The paper studies empirical-success ranking rules for saturation policies and non-asymptotic regret bounds, not confidence-set coverage.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Remove prop:rank-interval-projection as a numbered result and state it as an immediate reporting corollary beneath the coverage theorem.
Give the closure OEQ a worked K=3 nondegenerate response-table instance showing the intersection-null oracle, the induced lattice upper sets, and the desired strict containment target.

State a finite-instance complexity bound in terms of C, K, n, and |T| for the reference algorithm, even if it is exponential, to make the compression contribution auditable and distinguish it from labeled-schedule enumeration.
